display_name: PU-12M crew: seats, orders, callouts, tasks and world facts
status: P2 of docs/PU12_DEVELOPMENT.md. Read by simcore/crew_data.hpp; checked against data/procedures/pu12m.json.
notes: The crew of the PU-12M battery command post (docs/research/PU12_RESEARCH_2026-10.md). No source read gives the post's words of command or its reports: the phrasing is sam3d's in Soviet style, to be checked against the NVA plotters' handbook (nva_handbooks) and operator accounts. The task ids ready_halted and searching_on_march are the ones the NPC commander looks for (simcore/scenario_runner.hpp): for the post they mean deployed, and on the march with the radios and the gyro running.
source: ru_pu12_text (the crew by numbers); csla_pu12_manual and flak11 (the stations and their equipment); sam3d for the words

duties: Commands the post's crew and the battery
The ASPD-U and the IT-45, the commander-operator's place (rwd_mb3): marks targets with the DT-2 marker and the ДХ keypad, takes a cabled radar's targets off
Reads the plotting board for the long-range picture; hears the plotter call each new target
Gives the launchers their targets by voice on the battery net (FuG-4)
On the march, at the column's head: signals by flags and lamps; radio only for fire control while repelling an attack (voenizdat_osa_1991 pp. 232-239)
On the RTK-1: talks on the battery net (РСТ-4), hears the regiment's (РСТ-3) besides; the five lines
The main station of the battery net: designations, the spare frequency, duty reception, the launchers' read-backs
The regiment's telecode on the R-407 (FuG-5): its channel and its АПЧ (r407_plate); the R-111's antenna distributor on the SAU block at his place
seats.source: ru_pu12_text (командир боевого расчёта); flak11 (PU12-0: designations by voice, azimuth and range); csla_pu12_manual (his workplace)

duties: Hands out the radio data and checks that communications are ready (pvo_bu_ix_1984): «Связь готова»
Orients the post: the PAB-2 aiming circle, the GAK, the KP-4, the DTP
The R-123M FuG-1 (the air picture) beside him
Watches the covered unit's net (FuG-2) on PVS-2 and warns it on the commander's order
The IT-1 status board
Leads the crew's deployment and the march
seats.source: ru_pu12_text (No. 1); csla_pu12_manual (his workplace: KP-4, GAK panel, IT-1, DTP, R-123M)

duties: The plotting board: swings it open and folds it (its latch)
Writes on it what the regiment reads out on the air-picture net, report by report (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 23); not the tube, which is the commander's

Reports aloud to the commander, beside him, each new target as he writes it (number, bearing, range, height, identity, size), a turn and a target lost (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 23: plot_new, plot_turn, plot_lost); the commander decides on them (art. 17)
As the operator of pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 20: keeps and services the equipment, works the radio and the intercom, stands ready to replace the squad leader
No part in decisions in any source read: the commander decides (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 17); his voice is his reports
seats.source: ru_pu12_text (No. 2); rwd_mb3 (the plotter's place at the air-situation map; the tube's place, with the ФР block, is the commander's); pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 19, 20, 23 (radar units' regulation, an analogy: docs/research/PLOTTING_BOARD_2026-10.md)

duties: The R-111 FuG-3 on the regiment's net (r111_to); the R-123M FuG-4 of the battery net at his table and the RK-1U's data path
Listens to the air-picture net on FuG-1 through PVS-1 and reads each report out to the plotter (pvo_bu_x_1984 art. 23)
Raises and guys the mast
The distribution board and the rectifier
seats.source: ru_pu12_text (No. 3); csla_pu12_manual (his workplace); valka_pu12 (the signalman extends the mast)

duties: Drives the post
Sets out and runs the AB-1 generator set
The input board and the vehicle's power
On the intercom (PVS-3)
